```{python}
import _lib as L
import itables
itables.init_notebook_mode(all_interactive=False, connected=True)

k = L.csv("kandydaci.csv")
k.insert(1, "label_source", k["kategoria_final"].notna().map({True: "LLM", False: "rule"}))
k.insert(2, "form_changed", (k["forma_podstawowa"] != k["forma_kandydata"]).map({True: "yes", False: ""}))
front = ["forma_podstawowa", "forma_kandydata", "form_changed", "kategoria", "label_source", "pojecie", "obrazowalnosc", "dlugosc", "cls",
         "freq_cel", "freq_kontrast", "n_mat_cel", "n_przedmiotow", "freq_kwjp", "zipf_wordfreq"]
k = k[front + [c for c in k.columns if c not in front]]
n_llm = int((k["label_source"] == "LLM").sum())
chg = k[k["form_changed"] == "yes"]
n_chg = len(chg)
n_chg_words = int((chg["forma_podstawowa"].str.split().str.len() != chg["dlugosc"]).sum())
n_dup = int(k["forma_podstawowa"].duplicated(keep=False).sum())
```

`{python} f"{len(k):,}".replace(",", " ")` candidates passed the frequency filters. `{python} n_llm` of them were
labelled by the language models; the rest carry only the rule-based pre-label (`label_source` = `rule`), and
`do_llm` in `kategoria` means the rules could not decide either. None of the labels has been checked by a human.

::: {.callout-warning title="Two form columns"}
`forma_kandydata` is the string the statistics were computed for. `forma_podstawowa` is the same string unless the
language model returned a different base form: this happened for `{python} n_chg` candidates, and for
`{python} n_chg_words` of them the model's form has a different number of words (for example a single adjective
replaced by a whole two-word term), so the counts in the row do not describe the string in `forma_podstawowa`.
Because of these replacements `{python} n_dup` rows share their `forma_podstawowa` with another row. Filter
`form_changed` = `yes` to see them.
:::

Type in the boxes under the column names to filter a single column (for example `T3` under `kategoria`), click a
header to sort, and use **Columns** to show the hidden rank and per-model columns.

```{python}
L.source("kandydaci.csv")
L.glossary(k.columns)
```

```{python}
hidden = [c for c in k.columns if c.startswith("rank_")] + [
    "n_mat_kontrast", "n_klas_cel", "rozproszenie", "termopl_ok", "forma_podstawowa_llm", "kategoria_final",
    "ll_vs_kwjp", "log_ratio_kwjp"]
L.dt(k, order=[[list(k.columns).index("freq_cel"), "desc"]], hide=hidden, wrap=["pojecie"])
```
